mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the current month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 3.5% coincides with increased labor market rigidity, which raises the cost of capital and dampens equity valuation multiples, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Regression of 20-day SPX returns on UNRATE change shows positive coefficient with p < 0.05, or 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero when UNRATE crosses the threshold (t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (industrial production) grows at a rate exceeding 2% in two consecutive months, it indicates accelerating demand for goods, which anticipates a corporate earnings beat and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 20-day forward return does not exceed the mean of the previous 12 windows when the trigger occurs (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both INDPRO (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods price index) suggests supply-side softness, lowering market confidence and generating negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain non-negative in 80% of instances where both proxies decline (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a single month during a tightening cycle, the immediate effect is a term premium increase that reduces expected equity returns, producing a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
regime_hint: early stage of rate hike cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% (robust t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS (employment) of 2,000 or more suggests weakening labor demand, which elevates real interest rates via wage growth and reduces equity risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with PAYEMS declines at the 5% significance level (regression).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 1% above trend indicate strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with higher earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly > (trend + 1%) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5% confidence interval around the mean when RSAFS triggers (Granger causality test).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE and FEDFUNDS both increase simultaneously by at least 0.2% in the same month, it signals dual upward pressure on borrowing costs and wage growth, which compresses corporate profit margins and yields negative S&P 500 30-day forward returns.
regime_hint: coordinated policy and labor market tightening
failure_condition: 30-day forward returns remain non-negative in 70% of such trigger events (empirical frequency).
